transport: A failed tools/call is an MCP tool result with isError: true, never a JSON-RPC error object. The JSON-RPC error object is reserved for protocol-level faults (unparseable request, unknown method); a tool that failed on its own terms must stay visible to the model as tool output.
meta_key_note: The structured error object lives in the tool result's _meta under this key. _meta is part of the base MCP Result type from protocol version 2024-11-05 onward, and the key follows the MCP naming rule of a reverse-DNS-style prefix, a slash, and a name.
omit_when_empty_note: An error that carries no metadata produces no _meta member at all, so a server adopting this contract does not change the wire format of errors that have nothing to add.

fields.meaning: The tool's own stable error code. Consumers define the enum; corekit does not constrain its members.
The same text as the result's text content block, repeated so a client reading only the metadata has the whole failure.
fields.omitted_when: never, when the object is present at all

fields.meaning: Whether repeating the same call can plausibly succeed. Reported even when false: false is the actionable claim that a retry is wasted.
fields.omitted_when: the error does not implement the method

fields.meaning: Whether resuming needs a confirmed human action. A client may not derive an implicit takeover from anything else in this object.
fields.omitted_when: the error does not implement the method

fields.meaning: The single permitted next step after this failure.

fields.source_method: ErrorHint() string, else Hint() string, else exitcodes.CLIError.Hint

fields.meaning: Free-form machine-readable context the tool attaches to this failure class, for example replacement URL candidates found by a 404 recovery probe.

resolution: Every method is looked up with errors.As, so a wrapped error still reports the metadata of the error underneath. A corekit exitcodes.CLIError fills in code (from its Kind) and hint only where nothing more specific already did.
